get.description: Get Hypermedia links to resources accessible in GitHub's REST API

Lists all global security advisories that match the specified parameters. If no other parameters are defined, the request will return only GitHub-reviewed advisories that are not malware.

By default, all responses will exclude advisories for malware, because malware are not standard vulnerabilities. To list advisories for malware, you must include the `type` parameter in your request, with the value `malware`. For more information about the different types of security advisories, see "[About the GitHub Advisory database](https://docs.github.com/code-security/security-advisories/global-security-advisories/about-the-github-advisory-database#about-types-of-security-advisories)."

parameters.name: ghsa_id
parameters.description: If specified, only advisories with this GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier will be returned.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: If specified, only advisories of this type will be returned. By default, a request with no other parameters defined will only return reviewed advisories that are not malware.

parameters.name: cve_id
parameters.description: If specified, only advisories with this CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) identifier will be returned.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: If specified, only advisories for these ecosystems will be returned.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: If specified, only advisories with these severities will be returned.

parameters.name: cwes
parameters.description:
If specified, only advisories with these Common Weakness Enumerations (CWEs) will be returned.

Example: `cwes=79,284,22` or `cwes[]=79&cwes[]=284&cwes[]=22`

parameters.name: is_withdrawn
parameters.description: Whether to only return advisories that have been withdrawn.

parameters.name: affects
parameters.description:
If specified, only return advisories that affect any of `package` or `package@version`. A maximum of 1000 packages can be specified.
If the query parameter causes the URL to exceed the maximum URL length supported by your client, you must specify fewer packages.

Example: `affects=package1,package2@1.0.0,package3@2.0.0` or `affects[]=package1&affects[]=package2@1.0.0`

parameters.name: published
parameters.description:
If specified, only return advisories that were published on a date or date range.

For more information on the syntax of the date range, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."

parameters.name: updated
parameters.description:
If specified, only return advisories that were updated on a date or date range.

For more information on the syntax of the date range, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."

parameters.name: modified
parameters.description:
If specified, only show advisories that were updated or published on a date or date range.

For more information on the syntax of the date range, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."

parameters.name: epss_percentage
parameters.description:
If specified, only return advisories that have an EPSS percentage score that matches the provided value.
The EPSS percentage represents the likelihood of a CVE being exploited.

parameters.name: epss_percentile
parameters.description:
If specified, only return advisories that have an EPSS percentile score that matches the provided value.
The EPSS percentile represents the relative rank of the CVE's likelihood of being exploited compared to other CVEs.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The property to sort the results by.

get.description: Gets a global security advisory using its GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA) identifier.

Returns the GitHub App associated with the authentication credentials used. To see how many app installations are associated with this GitHub App, see the `installations_count` in the response. For more details about your app's installations, see the "[List installations for the authenticated app](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/apps#list-installations-for-the-authenticated-app)" endpoint.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

post.summary: Create a GitHub App from a manifest
post.description: Use this endpoint to complete the handshake necessary when implementing the [GitHub App Manifest flow](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/creating-github-apps-from-a-manifest/). When you create a GitHub App with the manifest flow, you receive a temporary `code` used to retrieve the GitHub App's `id`, `pem` (private key), and `webhook_secret`.

get.summary: Get a webhook configuration for an app
get.description:
Returns the webhook configuration for a GitHub App. For more information about configuring a webhook for your app, see "[Creating a GitHub App](/developers/apps/creating-a-github-app)."

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

patch.summary: Update a webhook configuration for an app
patch.description:
Updates the webhook configuration for a GitHub App. For more information about configuring a webhook for your app, see "[Creating a GitHub App](/developers/apps/creating-a-github-app)."

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

get.summary: List deliveries for an app webhook
get.description:
Returns a list of webhook deliveries for the webhook configured for a GitHub App.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

get.summary: Get a delivery for an app webhook
get.description:
Returns a delivery for the webhook configured for a GitHub App.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

post.summary: Redeliver a delivery for an app webhook
post.description:
Redeliver a delivery for the webhook configured for a GitHub App.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

permissions.title: App Permissions
permissions.description: The permissions granted to the user access token.

actions.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for GitHub Actions workflows, workflow runs, and artifacts.

administration.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for repository creation, deletion, settings, teams, and collaborators creation.

checks.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for checks on code.

contents.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for repository contents, commits, branches, downloads, releases, and merges.

deployments.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for deployments and deployment statuses.

environments.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for managing repository environments.

issues.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for issues and related comments, assignees, labels, and milestones.

metadata.description: The level of permission to grant the access token to search repositories, list collaborators, and access repository metadata.

packages.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for packages published to GitHub Packages.

pages.description: The level of permission to grant the access token to retrieve Pages statuses, configuration, and builds, as well as create new builds.

pull_requests.description: The level of permission to grant the access token for pull requests and related comments, assignees, labels, milestones, and merges.
